legal_notice: License findings are ORI's reading of fetched pages, not legal advice. Items marked legal_review need counsel before release.
rules: Every term records source and license.
Allowed sources: IFC names (reference with attribution), NIST SI usage, UCUM codes, QUDT quantity kinds, ORI-coined words and ORI property sets.
Never: ICC headings, ICC section organization, ICC definition text, MasterFormat, UniFormat, UNIFORMAT II, OmniClass (decision csi-classifications-excluded).
Candidate sources (Uniclass) are recorded with license evidence but supply no terms until adopted.
Defined terms in law are mapped by citation (defined at IRC R202, as adopted by VRC), never by copying the definition.
Plain names of physical things are used as is; code expression is re-expressed (decision plain-names-free).

decisions.decision: Keep using IFC 4.3 names: names only, with attribution, no definitions. Legal review before publication stays flagged.
Keep MasterFormat, UniFormat, OmniClass and UNIFORMAT II excluded until the MasterFormat appeal and the CSI contract (EULA) questions are settled.
decisions.revisit_when: the appeal from the reported 2026-09-01 C.D. Cal. ruling is resolved and CSI's contract terms are reviewed by counsel

decisions.decision: Evaluate Uniclass from its primary license pages; if open, record it as a candidate source with provenance; do not import terms.
decisions.outcome: Recorded as a candidate (CC BY-ND 4.0, tables only, not the API); zero terms imported; legal review flagged.

decisions.decision: Plain names for physical things (riser height, guard, smoke alarm, sink) are used as is; ORI does not coin substitutes. What ORI must not copy is the code's expression (sentence structure, ordering, selection). See docs/TERM-MERGER-METHOD-DRAFT.md; analysis to inform counsel, not a legal conclusion.

src:ifc-4.3.name: Industry Foundation Classes (IFC) 4.3 ADD2, entity, enumeration, property-set and quantity-set names

license_evidence.finding: Page states IFC is licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NoDerivatives 4.0 International.
CC BY-ND 4.0; also a legacy notice that the documentation may be used in software development with full attribution and that changes to the specification need prior written consent.
IFC 4.3 HTML documentation footer carries CC BY-ND 4.0.
IDS (Information Delivery Specification) repository is also CC BY-ND 4.0.

src:ifc-4.3.use_position: ORI-CL uses IFC names as identifiers (references to the published schema) with attribution. It does not copy IFC definitions or documentation text and does not modify or redistribute the specification. Whether identifier use can be an adaptation under the NoDerivatives term is flagged for legal review.

src:nist-si.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (US Government)

license_evidence.finding: NIST web information, except material marked as copyrighted, is public information that may be distributed or copied; byline credit requested.
Page reachable (HTTP 200); no separate copyright marking found on the landing page.

src:nist-si.use_position: Unit names, symbols and exact conversion factors (1 in = 0.0254 m) are facts; NIST is cited as the public-domain reference.

src:ucum.name: Unified Code for Units of Measure (UCUM) unit codes

license_evidence.finding: UCUM Copyright Notice and License 1.1 (June 2024): worldwide, non-exclusive, no-charge, royalty-free, revocable license to reproduce and distribute and to use the work for software that interoperates; attribution and notice conditions; trademark use not granted.

src:ucum.use_position: ORI-CL records the matching UCUM code for each unit (e.g. [in_i], [ft_i]) for interoperability only; the ORI-CL unit symbols themselves come from NIST usage. Revocability noted as an open question.

restricted_sources.name: MasterFormat

findings.finding: CSI FAQ: MasterFormat content is protected by copyright; use is under the MasterFormat EULA; commercial use in a derivative product employing MasterFormat numbers or titles requires contacting CSI.
CSI's authorized licensing channel states a license is required when CSI standards are used in revenue-generating services or software; software tools do not sublicense.

Trade press report: on 2026-09-01 a US District Court (C.D. Cal.) granted summary judgment to ZeroDocs, finding the asserted MasterFormat numbers, titles, divisions and taxonomy not protectable by copyright; the article notes contractual licensing and a possible appeal remain. Court order itself not fetched (UNVERIFIED primary).

restricted_sources.decision: Excluded from ORI-CL 0.1. Even after the reported 2026-09-01 ruling, CSI asserts copyright, trademark and contract terms, and an appeal is possible. Legal review before any reference.

findings.finding: CSI standards page for UniFormat (registered mark); no open license stated on the page.
Licensing channel states UniFormat elements in digital systems need a CSI Dynamic Standards license.
HTTP 403 to automated fetch; ASTM standards are sold under ASTM copyright (UNVERIFIED for this edition).

OmniClass single-user EULA: non-exclusive, non-transferable, terminable at any time; prohibits incorporating any portion into commercial construction software or information products provided to third parties; CSI retains all rights.
Connection failed (no HTTP response); not reachable for verification.

src:uniclass.name: Uniclass (NBS), classification tables as downloaded

license_evidence.finding: Download page: Uniclass is licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NoDerivatives 4.0 International (CC BY-ND 4.0); users and organizations may share and apply the tables on any personal or commercial project; users should not adapt the tables or add their own codes and should contact NBS to suggest changes. Latest tables dated July 2026.
NBS tool page (redirect from /our-tools/uniclass): Uniclass is free; all tables may be downloaded and used free of charge.

CC BY-ND 4.0 deed: share for any purpose, even commercially, and the freedoms are not revocable while the terms are followed; attribution requires credit, a link to the license and an indication of changes; a remixed, transformed or built-upon version may not be distributed.

The Uniclass API is under a separate licence: non-exclusive, revocable, non-transferable, for a permitted purpose; it bars derivative works and commercial distribution of API data without consent (cl. 3.7.5) and building a competing product (cl. 3.7.13). ORI would not use the API.
NBS website content is all rights reserved and not for commercial use without a licence; this covers site content, not the CC-licensed tables.
CC BY-ND is not among the licenses listed as conformant with the Open Definition (CC BY 4.0, CC BY-SA 4.0 and CC0 are). 'Open' here means free of charge and freely shareable, not freely modifiable.

src:uniclass.use_position: Candidate only; no terms imported. If adopted, ORI would reference Uniclass codes and titles verbatim, as unmodified identifiers with attribution to NBS and a link to CC BY-ND 4.0, in a separate mapping field next to ORI's own term (the same position as IFC names). ORI would not edit the tables, add its own codes to them, or use the NBS API. Uniclass content would stay under CC BY-ND 4.0; the repository's CC0 dedication cannot cover it.
legal_questions: Is a published ORI-term-to-Uniclass-code mapping an adaptation under the NoDerivatives term, or a reference to unmodified codes?
Can a CC0 repository carry CC BY-ND identifiers with a per-field license notice, as ORI already does for IFC names?
src:uniclass.uk_origin_note: Uniclass is a UK classification (built for UK practice); US residential fit is untested.
